reason: The displayed equality ||Rbar[x]||_quot = inf_{v in i*R*J} ||R(x+v)|| is false in general. The quotient norm of the output is inf_{w in i*R*J} ||R(x)+w||, whereas R vanishes on the vertical line, so inf_v ||R(x+v)|| = ||R(x)||; these need not agree. Concrete finite-dimensional model: X=R^2 with Euclidean norm, V=span(e1), R(e1)=0 and R(e2)=e1+e2. Then R kills V and induces Rbar, but for x=e2 one has ||Rbar[x]||_quot=1 while inf_{v in V}||R(x+v)||=sqrt(2). The desired bound is repairable by using, for every v in V, ||Rbar[x]||_quot=||[R(x+v)]||_quot <= ||R(x+v)|| <= ||R|| ||x+v|| and then infimizing, but the node's asserted equality/inference is invalid as written.
